messages:
marco-cs: hey @sarah-peopleops — quick payroll question. I updated my home address to Newmarket, NH on Feb 28 in Rippling but my 3/15 paycheck still had Massachusetts state withholding and the MBTA commuter deduction. NH has no wage tax, so this looks wrong. Can payroll refund the MA withholding and stop the commuter pre-tax going forward?

sarah-peopleops: thanks for flagging, marco. Can you confirm the effective move date (the date you started working from NH) and attach the updated address screenshot? I’ll tag payroll.

marco-cs: effective 2026-02-28 (first remote day from NH). attaching screenshot now — uploaded to Rippling under Profile > Address.

payroll-bot: payroll queue updated: ticket #PR-4682 created for state withholding review (auto-assigned to tom-payroll).

tom-payroll: got it. @marco-cs thanks — a couple quick notes: (1) NH has no state income tax so MA withholding after 2/28 is incorrect, (2) MBTA/commuter pre-tax is a MA regional benefit and should be stopped if your work location is outside MA. I can process an off-cycle correction to refund the MA state tax withheld since 3/1 and reverse the commuter deduction going forward.

marco-cs: appreciate it. Will I need to file anything with MA personally?

tom-payroll: likely we’ll issue a refund/adjustment on payroll side to return the withheld amount; for year-to-date issues we can either (A) do off-cycle refunds now and issue corrected paystubs, or (B) if small, you can claim the withheld tax when you file MA return for the year. I recommend option A so you have tidy paystubs. If MA already received withholding, they may want you to file for refund — we’ll include notes.

ashley-hr: @marco-cs can you also confirm your work location in Workday/Rippling is set to New Hampshire for tax jurisdiction? We need that flag for benefits and to stop commuter deductions. If not, I’ll update after you confirm address proof.

marco-cs: confirmed — work location = New Hampshire in Rippling. I uploaded the utility bill screenshot to the attachments.

tom-payroll: perfect. I’ll run an off-cycle on Friday (5 business days) to: 1) refund MA state tax withheld since 2026-03-01, 2) reverse MBTA commuter pre-tax deduction starting next pay period, 3) issue a corrected YTD paystub showing the change. If you need the funds sooner we can cut an off-cycle check but FYI there’s a small processing window.

marco-cs: Friday works. Please let me know the payroll run id once it’s done. Also curious if this will change W-2 — do you expect an amendment?

tom-payroll: if we fully correct the withholdings before year-end, your W-2 will reflect the corrected amounts and no W-2c should be necessary. If anything slips through, we’ll file a W-2c as needed and notify you. We’ll post the payroll run id here and attach the corrected stub in Rippling.

sarah-peopleops: I updated the HR ticket with the address proof and flagged for benefits. @ashley-hr can you confirm commuter benefit enrollment is paused so they don’t get deducted next cycle?

ashley-hr: done — paused MBTA/commuter elections for marco-cs effective next payday.

tom-payroll: PR-4682 update: scheduling off-cycle refund for 2026-03-19 payroll run id run-2026-03-19-PR4682. Expected net refund: $423.72 (MA state withholding + employer transit reversal). I’ll attach corrected stub after run.

marco-cs: thanks so much — that helps a lot.

sarah-peopleops: closing loop — please react with :white_check_mark: once you see the corrected stub. If anything else pops up we’ll reopen the ticket.

marco-cs: ✅ saw updated stub in Rippling and refund posted. All good from my side. Appreciate the quick help!
